title: Bitcoin whitepaper: transactions and peer-to-peer timestamping
text: Bitcoin is a peer-to-peer electronic cash system. Transactions are digitally signed, broadcast to the network, and timestamped by including them in a proof-of-work chain. Nodes accept blocks by validating their consensus rules, rather than relying on a central operator.

title: Bitcoin Developer Guide: block chain
text: The block chain is a public record of confirmed transactions. Each block references its predecessor, creating an ordered history. Full nodes independently validate blocks and transactions against their consensus rules.

title: Bitcoin Developer Guide: mining
text: Mining is the process of constructing candidate blocks and performing proof of work. Miners search for a block header hash below the network target. Proof of work makes rewriting confirmed history computationally expensive, while nodes still independently validate the block rules.

title: Bitcoin Developer Guide: wallets
text: A Bitcoin wallet manages keys and creates transactions. A wallet does not contain bitcoins; it stores or manages the information needed to spend outputs recorded on the blockchain. A seed phrase or private key must be kept secret.

title: Bitcoin Improvement Proposals
text: Bitcoin Improvement Proposals describe proposed standards, processes, and information for the Bitcoin ecosystem. A proposal's status and adoption must be checked individually; publication does not mean a proposal is active consensus policy.
